title: Keystone core schema with tenancy enforced in the database
scenario: Lumenfold's security review says tenancy in Keystone is enforced by PostgreSQL, not by every developer remembering a WHERE clause, and the CRM's validation rules become constraints an agent cannot route around. Write the first migration for accounts, contacts, opportunities and activities, with forced row-level security and indexes for the three hot queries, and prove it on real PostgreSQL (PGlite) with 87k seeded rows.
task: Model five tables with identity keys, composite (tenant_id, id) foreign keys and CHECK/UNIQUE business rules
Partial unique index for live contact emails, sf_id unique per tenant, GIN on custom_fields
RLS ENABLE + FORCE with USING and WITH CHECK on current_setting('app.tenant_id', true); NOLOGIN app role without BYPASSRLS
Indexes so the timeline, open-opportunities and custom-field queries avoid sequential scans as keystone_app
Explain the plans, including what happens to the GIN index under RLS, in ANSWER.md
acceptance: No tenant set: zero rows; tenant set: only own rows; cross-tenant inserts and updates rejected
Cross-tenant references impossible even as the owner; stage, amount, close-date and email rules enforced
No Seq Scan on the big tables for the three queries after ANALYZE
ANSWER.md quotes the plans and explains them
